name: Iceland
tagline: A geological work in progress, with a literary tradition older than most European states.
summary: Iceland sits on the seam between two continental plates, which is why it steams, erupts and rearranges itself. Three hundred and eighty thousand people live around the edge; the interior is uninhabited and closed by snow for most of the year. The sagas were written here in the 13th century and the language has changed so little that schoolchildren still read them.

season.note: June and July give near-permanent daylight and open highland roads. September is cheaper, emptier, and the aurora returns. Winter is workable on the south coast and unwise in the interior — the weather changes faster than the forecast.

getting_around: Ring Road 1 circles the island in 1,330 km and most visitors drive it. F-roads into the interior need a genuine 4x4 and are closed until late June. Check road.is and vedur.is every morning; Icelanders do.
food: Lamb that has spent the summer eating wild herbs on a mountain
Skyr, which is a cheese pretending to be a yoghurt
Hot dogs with crispy onions, defensible at any hour

festivals.name: Secret Solstice and the near-endless June light
Réttir — the autumn sheep round-up, done on horseback

know: Weather closes roads with little warning; a rental booked in July can still be stuck in a storm.
Off-road driving is illegal and damages moss that takes decades to regrow.
Tap water is glacial and free; buying it bottled is the most conspicuous tourist error in the country.

regions.name: Reykjavík & the Southwest
regions.summary: The capital, the tectonic rift you can walk into, and the geysers everyone drives to on day one.

cities.name: Reykjavík
cities.summary: The northernmost capital of a sovereign state, small enough to cross on foot and loud on Friday nights.
highlights: Hallgrímskirkja's basalt-column tower, and the view from the top
The Settlement Exhibition, built around a 10th-century longhouse found under the street
Neighbourhood geothermal pools — where Reykjavík actually socialises

experiences.name: The local pool, not the lagoon
experiences.summary: Every district has one: hot pots at different temperatures, a strict pre-shower rule, and the day's arguments happening in them.

cities.name: Þingvellir
cities.summary: A rift valley where the Atlantic plates pull apart, and where Iceland's parliament met in the open air from 930.
highlights: Walk the Almannagjá fissure between two continents
The Law Rock, where the Althing was proclaimed for eight centuries
Silfra: snorkelling in glacial meltwater with 100-metre visibility

experiences.name: Snorkel the Silfra fissure
experiences.summary: Two degrees, a dry suit, and water filtered through lava for decades — the clearest you will ever swim in.

regions.name: The South Coast & East
regions.summary: Waterfalls, black beaches, a glacier lagoon, and fjords that most Ring Road drivers rush.

cities.name: Vík í Mýrdal
cities.summary: A village of three hundred under a glacier, with black sand and dangerous surf.
highlights: Reynisfjara's basalt columns — and the sneaker waves that kill people who turn their backs
Dyrhólaey's arch and puffin colony in early summer
Katla under the ice, overdue and monitored

cities.name: Höfn & Jökulsárlón
cities.summary: A langoustine port beside Europe's largest ice cap, where icebergs float out to sea past a car park.
highlights: Jökulsárlón lagoon and the Diamond Beach opposite
Vatnajökull: 8% of the country, under ice
Langoustine, landed here and cooked simply

experiences.name: Into a glacier, in winter only
experiences.summary: The blue caves form and collapse each year; go with a guide who checks them that morning, and only from November to March.

regions.name: The Westfjords & North
regions.summary: The part almost nobody drives: bird cliffs, hot pots on empty shores, and whales off Skjálfandi.

cities.name: Ísafjörður
cities.summary: The Westfjords' capital: 2,700 people at the end of a fjord under a flat-topped mountain.
highlights: Hornstrandir, a roadless nature reserve reached by boat
Dynjandi, the waterfall that falls in seven tiers
Arctic foxes, which were here before anything else

cities.name: Húsavík
cities.summary: A wooden church, a whale museum, and the most reliable whale watching in Europe.
highlights: Humpbacks in Skjálfandi bay, April to October
The whale museum, built by the people who stopped hunting them

experiences.name: Whales from an old oak boat
experiences.summary: The refitted fishing schooners cut their engines and drift; the silence is half of what you came for.
